hypothesis: A rise above 10 percent in the average of the four most recently available weekly initial claims versus the preceding four weeks contains incremental information about a two-month unemployment rise of at least 0.2 pp.
training_clock: historical-origin frozen claims features and base UNRATE; labels initially available by current cut only
acceptance: at least5percent lower paired Brier than BOTH frequency baselines and strictly lower than persistence; no automatic prospective admission
missing_policy: exclude from all compared scores; no imputation, no nonconsecutive weeks, no revised-current-history substitution
retuning: none; threshold10percent, windows4+4weeks, prior12 and training60months fixed before evaluation
